1.meaning: An emphatic command meaning 'Declare the absolute transcendence and perfection of'—to proclaim that your Lord is utterly free from any flaw, partner, or deficiency. It is far stronger than mere praise; it actively negates from Allah anything unworthy of Him.

parts.en: glorify! / declare free of all imperfection!
helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before the next word

1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male ('you, glorify!'). The doubled middle letter (the shadda on the b) belongs to Form II, which here adds intensity and thoroughness to the act. The base command ends in a silent stop (sabbiḥ), but a small 'i' vowel is attached here only to smooth the join with the following word 'ism' (which begins with an unpronounced helping hamza); this 'i' carries no grammatical case meaning of its own.
1.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/move swiftly away; figuratively, to declare Allah far removed from all imperfection (to glorify)

2.meaning: The name—here 'the Name of your Lord,' meaning Allah's name by which He is invoked and remembered. To glorify the Name is to glorify the One who bears it.

parts.en: accusative ending ('-a'): marks it as the object of the verb

2.grammar: A singular noun functioning as the direct object of the command 'Glorify.' Its final '-a' vowel is the accusative case, which marks the thing being acted upon—what is being glorified. The opening alif is a 'connecting' hamza: it is written but not pronounced when the word is joined to what precedes it (hence 'sabbiḥi-sma' flows together).
2.root: Contested: the majority Kufan view derives it from و-س-م (w-s-m) — 'to mark, brand,' since a name marks out the thing it designates; the Basran view derives it from س-م-و (s-m-w) — 'height/loftiness,' since a name 'raises' and distinguishes what it names. و-س-م is the more widely accepted derivation.

3.meaning: 'Your Lord'—Rabb denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer, and Nurturer all at once: the One who creates, possesses, sustains, and brings every creature step by step to its completion. The attached 'your' makes it intimate and personal.

parts.en: genitive ending ('-i'): set up by the possessive link to 'your'

3.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun '-ka' meaning 'your' (addressing one male). The noun is in the genitive case (its '-i' vowel) because a following possessor pronoun puts it in a possessive construction ('the Lord OF you' = 'your Lord'). The doubled 'b' (shadda) is simply part of the root and is pronounced as a strengthened, held 'b.'
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, and have mastery over; hence Lord/Sustainer

4.meaning: 'The Most High'—the absolutely Exalted, higher than everything in rank, majesty, and being. As a description of the Lord, it affirms that He is supreme above all creation and above every limitation.
4.grammar: A definite adjective ('the Most High') describing 'your Lord,' built on the superlative pattern af'al ('most/-est'). It ends in a fixed long 'ā' written as a 'shortened alif' (alif maqṣūra), an ending that never changes for case—so no case vowel is pronounced. Because it describes the genitive 'your Lord,' it matches it in being definite. (The mark after it is a recitation pause sign, not part of the word.)

1.meaning: 'The One who…'—a relative pronoun ('he who,' 'the One that') that introduces a description. Here it points to the Lord and opens the clause telling what He did: 'who created and fashioned.'
1.grammar: A masculine singular relative pronoun, 'the one who.' It is a fixed, unchanging word (it takes no case endings) and must be followed by a clause that completes its meaning ('who created…'). Here it stands in apposition to 'your Lord,' i.e. it further identifies Him. Its form is permanently singular and masculine.

2.meaning: 'He created'—brought into existence out of nothing, originating the creation by His power.

parts.en: the final '-a' marks 'he' (3rd-person masculine) in the past tense

2.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base Form I, meaning 'he created.' With no attached subject pronoun, the bare form with final '-a' already means 'he' did it (third-person masculine singular). The action is completed/past. Its unstated subject is 'the One who' (the Lord) from the previous word.
2.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, originate, shape from nothing

3.meaning: '…and then proportioned (it)'—He shaped what He created in balanced, well-ordered measure, making each thing sound and complete, every part suited to its purpose.
3.grammar: The prefix 'fa-' means 'and then,' showing that this act follows the creating in order and consequence. 'Sawwā' is a past-tense Form II verb ('he proportioned/perfected'), where the doubled middle letter (shadda on the w) adds the sense of doing it thoroughly. It ends in a fixed long 'ā' (written as a shortened alif); this weak ending does not take a spoken case/mood vowel. The subject is still 'He' (the Lord).
3.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to make even, balanced, and well-proportioned

1.meaning: 'And the One who…'—joins a further description of the Lord to the previous one: 'and (He is) the One who…,' continuing the list of His acts.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' is the simple connector 'and,' linking this relative clause to the earlier 'the One who.' 'Alladhī' is again the masculine singular relative pronoun 'the one who'—a fixed form with no case endings—introducing another clause about what the Lord did ('who measured…').
1.root: — (connector 'wa-' plus relative pronoun; no triliteral root)

2.meaning: 'He measured out / decreed'—He determined each thing in exact measure: its nature, capacity, time, and destiny, ordaining everything precisely and wisely.

parts.en: the final '-a' marks 'he' (3rd-person masculine) in the past tense

2.grammar: A past-tense Form II verb, 'he measured out/decreed.' The doubled middle letter (shadda on the d) intensifies the sense—careful, precise determination. The bare form with final '-a' means 'he' performed it (third-person masculine singular), and the action is completed/past. The subject remains the Lord.
2.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — measure, capacity, decree, determining the precise extent of a thing

3.meaning: '…and then guided'—He directed each creature to what benefits it and to its purpose: animals to their sustenance and instincts, and human beings to the path of truth.

parts.en: he guided, directed (to the right way)

3.grammar: The prefix 'fa-' means 'and then,' showing this guiding follows the decreeing in sequence and as its result. 'Hadā' is a past-tense Form I verb ('he guided'). It ends in a fixed long 'ā' (written as a shortened alif), a weak ending that takes no spoken case/mood vowel. The unstated subject is still 'He' (the Lord).
3.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

1.meaning: 'And the One who…'—joins a further description of the Lord to the previous one: 'and (He is) the One who…,' continuing the list of His acts.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' is the simple connector 'and,' linking this relative clause to the earlier 'the One who.' 'Alladhī' is again the masculine singular relative pronoun 'the one who'—a fixed form with no case endings—introducing another clause about what the Lord did ('who measured…').
1.root: — (connector 'wa-' plus relative pronoun; no triliteral root)

2.meaning: 'He brought forth / produced'—He caused to come out and grow, here causing vegetation to spring from the earth.

parts.en: he brought out, produced, caused to emerge
the final '-a' marks 'he' (3rd-person masculine) in the past tense

2.grammar: A past-tense Form IV verb. Form IV (the prefixed 'a-' on the root) makes a verb causative—'to make something come out'—so from the root sense 'to go out' it means 'he brought forth.' The bare form with final '-a' means 'he' did it (third-person masculine singular), action completed/past. The subject is the Lord. (The translation 'brings forth' renders it as an ongoing truth, though the verb form itself is past.)
2.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, exit, emerge; Form IV: to bring/take out

3.meaning: 'The pasture'—green herbage and grazing growth; the vegetation that sprouts from the earth as food for grazing animals.
3.grammar: A definite noun ('the pasture') of the 'place/thing' pattern (maf'al), here naming what is grazed upon. It is the direct object of 'brought forth.' It ends in a fixed long 'ā' written as a shortened alif (alif maqṣūra), an ending that does not change for case, so the accusative is not shown by a spoken vowel. The 'al-' makes it definite ('the'). (The mark after it is a recitation pause sign.)
3.root: ر-ع-ي (r-ʿ-y) — to graze, pasture, tend; hence grazing-land/herbage

1.meaning: And then He made it / rendered it (into something). A past-tense verb of transformation: to make one thing become another, here referring to Allah turning the green pasture into dry chaff. The attached 'it' refers back to that vegetation.
1.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'He did it' — the subject is Allah, understood from context. The opening 'fa-' links it in sequence to the previous act ('He brought out the pasture... then made it...'). The attached '-hu' ('it/him') is the direct object, the thing being transformed. The verb 'jaʿala' takes two objects ('made X into Y'); here Y is the next word, ghuthāʾ.
1.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to render, to place

2.meaning: Withered, dried-out plant debris — the dead, brittle stalks and froth-like scum that floods leave behind; stubble or chaff. It pictures lush greenery reduced to worthless, lifeless refuse.
2.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, shown by the '-an' ending (the tanwīn, double-fatḥa). The accusative here marks it as the second object of 'jaʿala' — the state into which the vegetation was turned ('made it [into] withered chaff'). The '-an' also signals it is indefinite ('chaff', not 'the chaff').
2.root: غ-ث-و / غ-ث-ي (gh-th-w/y) — froth, scum, withered plant matter swept along by water

3.meaning: Dark, blackish-brown — the colour of vegetation once it has dried out and decayed. It describes the withered chaff as having turned a dusky, dark hue, the look of dead and rotting growth.
3.grammar: An adjective of colour on the pattern afʿal (the pattern used for colours and bodily traits, e.g. aḥmar 'red'). It describes the preceding 'ghuthāʾ' (the chaff), so it is accusative to agree with it. Its visible ending, however, comes from its weak final root letter: the word ends in alif maqṣūra ('-ā'), so its surface ending stays a fixed long '-ā' and does not show a separate case-vowel. Separately, words on the afʿal colour pattern are also diptote — meaning that when a case-vowel would show, they take fatḥa (not kasra) in the genitive and never take tanwīn — but that is a distinct fact from the invariable '-ā' you see here, which is caused by the weak ending.
3.root: ح-و-ي / ح-و-ى (ḥ-w-y) — to be dark/dusky brown-black

1.meaning: We will make you recite / We will have you read aloud. A future-tense promise from Allah (speaking as 'We' of majesty) to the Prophet that He will cause him to recite the revelation, so that it is preserved in his heart. The 'you' addressed is the Prophet.
1.grammar: A present/future verb made future by the prefix 'sa-' ('will'). It is in the causative (Form IV) pattern, so it means not 'we recite' but 'we make [someone] recite.' The 'nu-' prefix marks the subject as 'we' (the divine 'We' of majesty). The verb's base vowel ending is '-u', the normal indicative ('a plain statement of fact'). The attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (masculine singular), i.e. the Prophet whom Allah will cause to recite.
1.root: ق-ر-أ (q-r-ʾ) — to read, to recite (the root of 'Qurʾān')

2.meaning: So... not / and so not. A linking word 'so/then' joined to the negative 'not', introducing the consequence of the preceding promise: '...so that you will not (forget).'
2.grammar: Two particles. 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', showing that what follows is the result of 'We will make you recite.' 'lā' is the negative particle 'not'. Together they introduce the negated outcome ('so you will not forget'). Particles like these have no case or tense endings of their own.

3.meaning: You forget / you will forget. A verb addressed to the Prophet, here negated: he will not lose or let slip from memory the revelation given to him.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb, second-person masculine singular ('you'), shown by the 'ta-' prefix. Negated by the preceding 'lā' ('you will not forget'). Because its root ends in a weak letter, the verb closes in a fixed long '-ā' rather than a short case-vowel; this long ending is its indicative/unchanged form here. The promise is that forgetting will not happen.

1.meaning: Except / unless / save for. A particle that carves out an exception from what was just said: 'you will not forget — except (for) whatever Allah wills.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally 'in' 'if' + 'lā' 'not', fused into one word). It makes an exception to the preceding statement, introducing the one case that is set apart. It carries no case or tense ending of its own; what follows it is the thing excepted.

2.meaning: What / whatever / that which. A word standing in for an unnamed thing — here, 'whatever (Allah wills)'. It points to an unspecified matter rather than naming it.
2.grammar: A relative pronoun meaning 'what / that which', used here for non-human things. It introduces the clause 'what Allah wills' and serves as the exception after 'illā'. As an indeclinable particle-like word, it never changes its ending for case or number; it simply links to the verb that follows.

3.meaning: He willed / He wished — i.e. He chose and decreed. A past-tense verb expressing Allah's sovereign will: that which He determines and intends to come about.
3.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'He willed.' The final '-a' is the standard past-tense ending for 'he'. Although past in form, in this context it carries the sense 'whatever He wills,' covering Allah's ongoing will. Its subject is the next word, 'Allah.'
3.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, to wish, to intend

4.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God, the sole Creator and Lord worshipped in Islam. It is His unique personal name, not a common noun, and has no plural or feminine form.
4.grammar: The divine name, here in the nominative case, shown by the final '-u'. The nominative marks it as the doer/subject of the verb 'shāʾa' — Allah is the One who wills ('whatever Allah wills'). The '-u' is the subject-marker ending.
4.root: — (proper name; sometimes linked to ʾ-l-h 'to be worshipped/deity')

5.meaning: Indeed He / Truly, He. An emphasizing particle 'indeed/truly' with the attached pronoun 'He' (Allah). It opens a statement with assurance and force: 'He most certainly...'
5.grammar: Begins with 'inna', an emphatic particle that strengthens and confirms the whole sentence ('indeed, truly, surely'). It has no exact one-word English match — its job is to add certainty. Grammatically, 'inna' governs the noun or pronoun after it in the accusative; this first element is called its 'ism' (its 'noun'). Here that element is the attached '-hu' ('He', referring to Allah), so '-hu' is the accusative-form pronoun standing as the ism of 'inna'. The predicate that completes the statement — the 'khabar' of 'inna' — is the following verb 'yaʿlamu' ('He knows'). So the full sense is 'Indeed He [Allah] knows.'
5.root: — ('inna' is a particle; '-hu' is a pronoun — no root)

6.meaning: He knows. A present-tense verb stating that Allah possesses complete, continuous knowledge — here, of all that is spoken openly and all that is concealed.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('He'), marked by the 'ya-' prefix. The final '-u' is the indicative ending — a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('He knows'). Its subject is 'He' (Allah, from the previous 'innahu'); grammatically this whole verb serves as the predicate (khabar) of the preceding 'inna'. Present tense here conveys constant, unceasing knowledge.

7.meaning: That which is openly said or done — speech and action made loud, public, and out in the open, as opposed to what is concealed. Here it points to everything human beings make manifest.

parts.en: accusative ending (object of the verb 'He knows')

7.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' (fatḥa) is the accusative case: it marks this word as the direct object of the verb 'He knows' — Allah 'knows the open/manifest.'
7.root: ج-ه-ر (j-h-r) — to be open, loud, public; to speak or act openly

8.meaning: 'And what…' — joins to the previous phrase and introduces a second thing known to Allah. Here 'mā' is a relative pronoun meaning 'that which / whatever,' setting up the clause 'what is hidden.'
8.grammar: Two particles joined together. 'wa' is the connector 'and.' 'mā' is a relative pronoun, 'what / that which,' standing for an unstated thing and introducing the verb that follows ('what is hidden'). Particles do not take case endings, so there is no final-vowel case to mark.

9.meaning: It is hidden / stays concealed — something kept out of sight or unseen, the counterpart to 'the manifest' in the same verse.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular: 'he/it is hidden.' The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it' and ongoing present action. The verb ends in a long '-ā' (a 'defective' verb whose final root letter is a weak vowel-letter), so the case/mood vowel is not pronounced as a separate sound; the subject is 'what (mā)' from the previous word — 'and what is hidden.'
9.root: خ-ف-ي (kh-f-y) — to be hidden, concealed, unseen

1.meaning: And We will make it easy for you / smooth your way — Allah promising to facilitate and ease the Prophet's path. The attached 'you' is the one being eased.
1.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the intensive (form II) pattern, meaning 'to make easy, facilitate.' The 'nu-' prefix means 'We' (the royal/divine 'We'). The '-u' ending is the indicative mood: it states a plain fact or promise — 'We will surely ease.' The attached '-ka' is the object pronoun 'you' (masculine singular), so: 'We will ease you / make it easy for you.'

2.meaning: Toward the easiest way / the path of greatest ease — a noun naming 'the easiest state or way,' here the way of ease and goodness toward which the Prophet is guided.
2.grammar: A noun with the prefix 'li-' ('to / toward') and the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The word is a feminine superlative pattern, 'the easiest (way).' It ends in a long '-ā' (a fixed final vowel-letter), so it does not show a separate case sound; the prefix 'li-' supplies the sense of direction/purpose — 'toward the easiest way.'

1.meaning: So remind! / give the reminder! — a command to admonish and call to mind, i.e. to preach and exhort. The opening 'fa' ('so/then') links it as a consequence of what preceded.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb in the intensive (form II) pattern: 'remind, admonish, exhort.' It is addressed to a single male ('you'). The verb ends on a silent final consonant (jussive/command form, no added vowel), which is exactly how a direct order is formed. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'so/then,' drawing a conclusion: 'So remind!'
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind; reminder

2.meaning: 'If' — a conditional particle introducing a condition: it sets up 'if X, then Y.' Here: 'if the reminder benefits…'.
2.grammar: A conditional particle, 'if.' It introduces a condition whose fulfillment is left open. It is a particle and takes no case ending; it simply governs the conditional clause that follows ('if the reminder benefits').

3.meaning: It brought benefit / proved useful — the act of doing good or being profitable to someone. Here: 'if the reminder benefits.'

parts.en: carried-over 'n' of the preceding 'in' (assimilated into this verb's opening nūn)
it benefited (Form I verb stem نَفَعَ)
she/it (feminine past-tense ending), here read '-ati' before the next word

3.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person feminine singular: 'it benefited.' This is a plain Form I verb, نَفَعَ (nafaʿa); it is NOT the intensive/doubled (Form II) pattern. The doubled 'n' (shadda) at the start is not a doubled root letter — it is the 'n' of the preceding particle 'in' assimilating (idghām) into the verb's own opening nūn. The '-at' ending marks a feminine singular subject (the subject is 'al-dhikrā,' 'the reminder,' which is feminine); its final 't' is normally silent but is here voiced as '-ati' to link smoothly to the next word beginning with 'al-.' Although the sense is a general/future condition ('if it benefits'), the verb form itself is past tense, as Arabic conditions often use.
3.root: ن-ف-ع (n-f-ʿ) — to benefit, profit, be of use

4.meaning: The reminder / the admonition — the act or means of bringing truth to mind; in context, the Qur'anic reminder that calls people to heed Allah.

parts.en: the (definite article; its 'l' assimilates into the sun letter 'dh,' doubling it)

4.grammar: A feminine noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'); the 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the 'dh' (a 'sun letter'), so it is pronounced as a doubled 'dh' ('adh-dhikrā'). The single dhāl belongs to the noun stem and is written once; the article segment carries the assimilated/doubled 'dh' and the stem that follows is 'krā.' The word ends in a fixed long '-ā,' so it shows no separate case sound. It is the subject of the verb 'benefited' — 'if the reminder benefits.'
4.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind; reminder

1.meaning: He will take heed / become mindful — to receive the reminder, reflect, and be admonished by it. The 'sa-' makes it future: 'he will pay heed.'
1.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, in a reflexive pattern ('to let oneself be reminded,' i.e. take heed). The 'sa-' prefix means 'will' (near future); 'ya-' marks 'he.' The original 't' of this verb-pattern has merged into the root's 'dh,' giving the doubled 'dh' sound. The '-u' ending is the indicative mood — a plain statement: 'He will take heed.' Its subject is 'man' ('the one who…') in the next word.
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind; reminder

2.meaning: 'The one who / whoever' — a relative pronoun standing for a person, here introducing 'the one who fears Allah.'
2.grammar: A relative pronoun referring to a person, 'the one who / whoever.' It is the subject of 'will take heed' and is itself described by the following verb ('who fears'). As a pronoun it has a fixed form and takes no case ending.

3.meaning: He fears / stands in reverent awe — a fear mixed with reverence and awareness of Allah's greatness, not mere fright. Here: 'the one who fears (Allah).'

parts.en: he (present-tense prefix, 3rd person masc.; its 'y' is doubled in recitation after the preceding word)

3.grammar: A present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular: 'he fears, holds in reverent awe.' The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he' and ongoing/present action. The verb ends in a long '-ā' (a 'defective' verb with a weak final root letter), so it shows no separate mood vowel. It describes 'man' ('the one who'): 'the one who fears (Allah).'
3.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — to fear with reverence and awe

1.meaning: And he will keep away from it / shun it — the verb describes someone deliberately steering clear of something and putting distance between himself and it. Here the 'it' refers to the reminder (the message), which the wretched person avoids.

parts.en: it (referring to a feminine noun, here 'the reminder')

1.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 'he' form (3rd person masculine singular). It is built on a reflexive-intensive pattern (form V, tafa''ala) that adds the sense of 'making oneself' avoid — i.e. deliberate self-distancing. The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he', and the final '-u' ending is the indicative mood, the normal ending for a simple statement of fact ('he avoids / will avoid'). The attached 'hā' is the object 'it'.
1.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side; to be at the side of, hence to put to one side / keep away from

2.meaning: The most wretched / most miserable one — the person sunk deepest in misery and ruin. It is the superlative of 'shaqī' (wretched, doomed to hardship), describing the most unfortunate of people, the one destined for the Fire.
2.grammar: A superlative adjective ('most wretched') on the pattern af'al, used here as a noun ('the most wretched one'). The 'al-' prefix is 'the', making it definite — the specific wretched person. The word ends in a fixed long '-ā' (alif maqṣūra) that does not change for case; such superlatives are indeclinable, so the ending carries no case vowel of its own. It functions as the subject of the previous verb ('he will shun it' = 'the most wretched will shun it').
2.root: ش-ق-و / ش-ق-ي (sh-q-w/y) — wretchedness, misery, hardship (opposite of felicity)

1.meaning: 'The One who…'—a relative pronoun ('he who,' 'the One that') that introduces a description. Here it points to the Lord and opens the clause telling what He did: 'who created and fashioned.'
1.grammar: A masculine singular relative pronoun, 'the one who.' It is a fixed, unchanging word (it takes no case endings) and must be followed by a clause that completes its meaning ('who created…'). Here it stands in apposition to 'your Lord,' i.e. it further identifies Him. Its form is permanently singular and masculine.

2.meaning: He will burn in / be roasted by (the Fire) — the verb means to enter a blazing fire and be scorched and consumed by its heat, to roast in it. It conveys suffering the full searing punishment of the Fire.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 'he' form (3rd person masculine singular): 'he will burn.' The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he.' The verb has a weak final letter, so instead of a short case vowel it ends in a long '-ā'; in this indicative (statement) form the ending stays as '-ā'. It takes a direct object ('the Fire') in the next word.
2.root: ص-ل-ي (ṣ-l-y) — to roast, scorch, burn in fire

3.meaning: The Fire — the blazing fire of Hell, the place of punishment. Here it is the thing that is entered and burned in.

parts.en: accusative ('-a') ending — marks it as the object

3.grammar: A feminine noun meaning 'the Fire.' The 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case: it marks 'the Fire' as the direct object of the verb before it — 'he will burn (in) THE FIRE.'
3.root: ن-ي-ر (n-y-r) — fire; to burn, blaze. (Note: نار 'fire' and نور 'light' are cognate, but 'light' belongs to the related root ن-و-ر; 'fire' itself is not a meaning of ن-و-ر.)

4.meaning: The greatest / the great(est) one — the superlative 'biggest, greatest' in the feminine form, here describing the Fire as the supreme, most terrible Fire.
4.grammar: A feminine superlative adjective ('the greatest'), on the pattern fu'lā, describing the feminine noun 'the Fire.' The 'al-' is 'the,' matching the definiteness of 'the Fire.' It ends in a fixed long '-ā' (alif maqṣūra); words of this superlative pattern do not take changing case vowels, so the ending is invariable. As an adjective it agrees with 'the Fire' in being feminine and definite.
4.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, bigness; to be great/large

1.meaning: Then / thereafter — a connecting word that links what follows to what came before, with a sense of sequence and often of some interval or a step up in seriousness ('then, after that'). Here it moves to the further fact that in the Fire he neither dies nor lives.
1.grammar: A connecting particle (conjunction) meaning 'then, after that.' Unlike a plain 'and,' it implies order and usually a gap or progression between the two things joined. It is a fixed function word with no case ending and does not change form.

2.meaning: Not — a particle of negation. Paired with a present-tense verb it denies the action ('does not / will not …'). Here it negates 'die': he will not die.
2.grammar: A negating particle. Placed before a present/future verb, it simply negates it without changing the verb's ending ('he does/will not …'). It is a fixed function word with no case or inflection of its own.

3.meaning: He dies / he will die — the verb 'to die,' the ceasing of life. In this verse it is negated: he will not die (and so find relief from the punishment).
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 'he' form (3rd person masculine singular): 'he dies / will die.' The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he.' The final '-u' ending is the indicative mood, the standard ending for a plain statement. Standing after the negative 'lā,' the whole phrase means 'he will not die.'

4.meaning: In it / therein — the preposition 'in' joined to 'it,' referring back to the Fire: 'in it (the Fire).'
4.grammar: A preposition ('in') with an attached pronoun ('it'). The pronoun 'hā' means 'it' for a feminine noun, here 'the Fire.' Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; 'hā' has one fixed form, so it shows no separate vowel change. Together: 'in it / therein.'

5.meaning: And not — the joining word 'and' combined with the negation 'not,' continuing a denial: 'and (he does) not …' Here it adds the second half: nor will he live.
5.grammar: Two joined function words: 'wa' ('and') plus 'lā' ('not'). The 'wa' connects this clause to the previous one, and 'lā' negates the following present-tense verb without altering its ending. Neither word inflects for case. The pairing 'lā … wa-lā …' gives the English 'neither … nor …' — neither dies nor lives.

6.meaning: He lives / he will live — the verb 'to live,' to have life. Negated here: nor will he (truly) live — so he is caught between, neither released by death nor granted real life.
6.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, 'he' form (3rd person masculine singular): 'he lives / will live.' The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he.' The verb has a weak final letter, so it ends in a long '-ā' rather than a short vowel; in this indicative (statement) form the ending remains '-ā.' After the preceding 'wa-lā,' it means 'and he will not live.'
6.root: ح-ي-ي / ح-ي-و (ḥ-y-y/w) — life; to live, to be alive

1.meaning: Certainly / indeed — an emphasis particle. Before a past-tense verb it stresses that the action has definitely and fully happened ('has surely …'); here it underlines the certainty of 'has succeeded' (he has truly succeeded).
1.grammar: An emphasizing particle. Placed before a past-tense verb, it affirms that the act is realized and certain — strengthening it to 'has indeed / has surely done.' It is a fixed function word with no case ending and does not change form.

2.meaning: He has truly succeeded / attained salvation and lasting well-being. The verb conveys reaching a state of flourishing, deliverance, and prosperity — not mere worldly success but the deep, enduring success of the soul that thrives. In the verse it is fronted for emphasis: 'Successful indeed is the one who...'
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he succeeded / has succeeded.' The final -a is simply the built-in ending of this past-tense form (it is not a case ending). Being Form IV (the af'ala pattern, here with the prefixed hamza 'a-'), it carries the sense of fully entering into or attaining the state of the root — i.e. coming into success/flourishing. Used here to declare a settled, accomplished fact about the one who purifies himself.
2.root: ف-ل-ح (f-l-ḥ) — to split/till the soil, hence to cultivate and thereby thrive, prosper, succeed

3.meaning: 'The one who / whoever' — a relative pronoun standing for a person, here introducing 'the one who fears Allah.'
3.grammar: A relative pronoun referring to a person, 'the one who / whoever.' It is the subject of 'will take heed' and is itself described by the following verb ('who fears'). As a pronoun it has a fixed form and takes no case ending.

4.meaning: He purified himself — cleansing his soul of sin and disbelief and causing it to grow in faith and righteousness. The word joins two ideas: removing impurity and increasing in goodness (the same root underlies zakāt, the purifying portion of wealth). It points to inward self-purification and spiritual growth.

parts.en: reflexive/Form V prefix (showing the action falls back on oneself)

4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he purified himself.' It is Form V (tafa''ala) — the doubled middle letter (-kk-) intensifies the action, and the ta- prefix makes it reflexive, so the purifying is something he does to and for his own self. The final long -ā is the verb's own ending for 'he' on a root ending in a weak/vowel letter (it stands where a normal -a would be); it is not a case marker. The sense is settled and completed: he has accomplished this self-purification.
4.root: ز-ك-و / ز-ك-ي (z-k-w) — purity together with growth/increase; to be clean and to flourish

1.meaning: And he called to mind / made mention of — i.e. remembered with the heart and on the tongue. The root spans both silent remembrance and spoken commemoration. In the verse it is 'remembered the Name of his Lord,' keeping Allah present in mind and invoking Him.
1.grammar: Connector 'wa' (and) joined to a past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'and he remembered.' This is the plain Form I verb. The final -a is the built-in past-tense ending for 'he' (not a case ending). It reports a completed act, paired with the preceding verbs (purified... and remembered... and prayed) as marks of the successful person.
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, call to mind, mention, invoke

2.meaning: The name—here 'the Name of your Lord,' meaning Allah's name by which He is invoked and remembered. To glorify the Name is to glorify the One who bears it.

parts.en: accusative ending ('-a'): marks it as the object of the verb

2.grammar: A singular noun functioning as the direct object of the command 'Glorify.' Its final '-a' vowel is the accusative case, which marks the thing being acted upon—what is being glorified. The opening alif is a 'connecting' hamza: it is written but not pronounced when the word is joined to what precedes it (hence 'sabbiḥi-sma' flows together).
2.root: Contested: the majority Kufan view derives it from و-س-م (w-s-m) — 'to mark, brand,' since a name marks out the thing it designates; the Basran view derives it from س-م-و (s-m-w) — 'height/loftiness,' since a name 'raises' and distinguishes what it names. و-س-م is the more widely accepted derivation.

3.meaning: Of his Lord — 'Lord' (Rabb) meaning the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings His servant to maturity. The attached 'his' ties this lordship to the individual believer: the One who is his own Sustainer and Caretaker.
3.grammar: A noun, 'Lord,' with the attached pronoun '-hi' meaning 'his.' The -i vowel on the stem (rabb-i) is the genitive case, which here does two jobs at once: it shows possession with the following pronoun ('Lord OF his' = his Lord) and reflects that the whole phrase is itself governed by the earlier word 'Name' ('the Name OF his Lord'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (with an i-vowel) precisely because it follows that genitive -i.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship that raises and cares for

4.meaning: And he prayed / performed the prayer — specifically the ritual Prayer (ṣalāh). The root carries the sense of invocation and supplication, and in Islamic usage it denotes the formal worship of bowing and prostration. Here it crowns the list: he purified himself, remembered his Lord, and prayed.

parts.en: he prayed / performed the Prayer (intensive stem)

4.grammar: The connector 'fa-' (and then / and so, suggesting it follows on from the remembrance) joined to a past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular: 'and he prayed.' It is Form II (fa''ala) — the doubled middle letter (-ll-) marks this dedicated, intensive sense of performing worship. The final long -ā is the verb's ending for 'he' on a root ending in a weak/vowel letter (standing in for the usual -a); it is not a case marker. It states a completed act.
4.root: ص-ل-و / ص-ل-ي (ṣ-l-w) — supplication and worship; the formal ritual Prayer

1.meaning: A particle of rebuttal and redirection, roughly 'nay' or 'rather / on the contrary.' It does not translate to a single content word; its job is to set aside or correct what came before (or the listener's assumption) and turn attention to a truer point — here, exposing that people instead prefer this fleeting world.
1.grammar: A particle (a function word), not a noun or verb, so it has no case or tense and never changes form. Its sukūn (the silent mark on the final letter) means it ends without a vowel. Grammatically it pivots the discourse — dismissing or qualifying the preceding idea and introducing the contrasting reality that follows.

2.meaning: You (all) give preference to / choose over something else. The verb means to favor one thing above another, to prefer and prioritize it. In the verse the reproach is that 'you prefer' the life of this world (over the Hereafter).

parts.en: prefer / give preference (Form IV stem; the hamza ؤ is the af'ala prefix consonant)

2.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, second-person masculine plural: 'you (all) prefer.' The prefix tu- signals 'you' in the present tense; the hamza (ؤ, a glottal stop transliterated ') is the Form IV af'ala prefix consonant, which is why the stem is -'thiru; and the ending '-ūna' marks a plural masculine subject ('you all') while also being the full, un-clipped form that shows the verb is in the plain indicative mood (a simple statement of fact, here an accusation). Being Form IV (af'ala) gives the transitive sense 'to give preference to.' Reading 'you' rather than 'they' follows the canonical recitation of this word.
2.root: ء-ث-ر (’-th-r) — to favor, prefer, give precedence; to leave a mark/trace

3.meaning: The (worldly) life — life as lived in this present existence. The word denotes 'life' in the sense of living, vitality, the state of being alive, here pointing to the temporal life of this world that people wrongly prioritize.

parts.en: accusative ending (marks it as the object)

3.grammar: A noun, 'the life,' carrying 'the' (al-) at the front. The final -a is the accusative case, which marks it as the direct object of the verb — it is the thing being preferred ('you prefer the life'). (The written tā' marbūṭa is pronounced as a hard -t before this case ending: ḥayāta.)
3.root: ح-ي-و / ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-w) — life, to live, vitality

4.meaning: The nearer / lower world — literally 'the nearest, closest one,' an adjective used as a name for this present world because it is the life immediately at hand, as opposed to the Hereafter which is yet to come. It carries an undertone of 'lower' and lesser in worth.
4.grammar: An adjective in the feminine superlative form (dunyā = 'nearest/lowest'), with 'the' (al-) at the front; the l of al- assimilates into the following d, so it is pronounced ad-dunyā. It describes the preceding noun 'the life,' so it follows that noun's accusative case — but because the word ends in a long -ā it cannot show a vowel ending, so its case is silent/unmarked (grammatically accusative, matching 'the life'). Together: 'the life of this nearer world.'
4.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, to be close/low; hence 'this world' as the nearer life

1.meaning: And the Hereafter — 'the last/final (abode),' an adjective used as a name for the everlasting life to come after this world, the ultimate and concluding existence. It is set in contrast to 'this nearer world.'

parts.en: nominative ending (marks it as the subject)

1.grammar: Connector 'wa' (here meaning 'while/whereas,' drawing a contrast) plus the noun 'the Hereafter' with 'the' (al-) at the front. The final -u is the nominative case, marking this word as the subject of its sentence — 'the Hereafter (is) better...' (The written tā' marbūṭa is pronounced as a hard -t before the ending: ākhiratu.)
1.root: ء-خ-ر (’-kh-r) — to be last, to come after; hence 'the Hereafter,' the final abode

2.meaning: Better — superior and more excellent. In origin the word means 'good,' but in this comparative usage it carries the force of 'better / best,' i.e. more good than the alternative. Here: the Hereafter is better (than this world).
2.grammar: A noun/adjective serving as the comparative 'better.' Morphologically it IS the af'al elative form of the root: khayr is the regularly contracted form of akhyar (أَخْيَر), the contraction that standardly happens to hollow roots (those with a weak middle letter) in the af'al pattern — so it carries the comparative force without displaying the full af'al shape on the surface. It is the predicate — the word that tells us about the subject 'the Hereafter.' The ending '-un' is the nominative case (matching its subject) together with tanwīn (the doubled vowel marking it as indefinite, 'better' rather than 'the better'). So: 'the Hereafter is better.'
2.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — goodness, good; that which is choice and excellent

3.meaning: And more lasting / more enduring — 'more everlasting,' that which remains and abides longer. The word stresses permanence and continuance: the Hereafter not only is better but also outlasts this passing world, indeed endures forever.
3.grammar: Connector 'wa' (and) joined to the comparative adjective abqā, 'more lasting / more enduring' (the af'al comparative pattern, with the prefixed 'a-' giving the sense 'more...'). It is a second predicate of 'the Hereafter,' so it is grammatically nominative; but because the word ends in a long -ā it cannot display a vowel ending, so its case is silent/unmarked. Together with the previous word: 'the Hereafter is better and more lasting.'
3.root: ب-ق-ي / ب-ق-و (b-q-y) — to remain, last, endure, abide

1.meaning: An emphatic opening particle that has no clean English equivalent. It introduces a sentence with a strong assertion, roughly 'Indeed' or 'Truly' — vouching that what follows is certainly the case. It also grammatically governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the accusative.
1.grammar: This is a particle, so it has no tense or person. It is one of the 'sisters of inna': it grips the following noun and forces it into the accusative case (its 'subject'), while the predicate stays in the nominative. Its whole job is emphasis — it tells the listener 'take this as certain.' The doubled -nn (shadda) is part of the word itself, not an ending.

2.meaning: The near demonstrative 'this' — pointing to something close at hand or just mentioned. Here it points to the message/teaching of the preceding verses, as if to say 'this very thing.'

parts.en: this (masculine singular, the thing pointed at)

2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, 'this (one).' Demonstratives in Arabic are largely fixed in form — they do not take the usual case-vowel endings, so the final -ā does not change for case here. Because inna precedes it, hādhā functions as the emphasized subject ('Indeed THIS…').

3.meaning: A two-part word meaning 'surely is in.' It combines an emphasis prefix ('surely / certainly') with the preposition 'in,' stressing that the thing truly is located within what follows.
3.grammar: The la- prefix is the 'lām of emphasis' that typically pairs with inna to double down on the assertion ('inna… la…' = 'Indeed… surely…'). Attached to it is the preposition fī ('in'). As a preposition, fī itself takes no case; instead it puts the noun after it into the genitive case (which is why the next word ends in -i).

4.meaning: 'The scriptures / the written pages.' The plural of ṣaḥīfa, a sheet or page on which something is written — here the revealed Books of earlier prophets.
4.grammar: A definite plural noun. The -i ending is genitive, caused by the preposition fī before it ('in THE scriptures'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates in sound into the following ṣ (a 'sun letter'), which is why it is pronounced ṣ-ṣuḥuf even though it is written with lām.
4.root: ص-ح-ف (ṣ-ḥ-f) — writing on a page / a written sheet

5.meaning: 'The former / the earlier ones.' A feminine adjective describing the scriptures as the first and earliest, i.e. the Books revealed before the Qur'an.
5.grammar: A definite adjective, feminine singular, agreeing with the plural 'scriptures' (non-human plurals take feminine-singular agreement in Arabic). Although it stands in a genitive phrase, this word ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case, so no separate case vowel is shown. It describes the ṣuḥuf as 'the earlier' ones.

1.meaning: 'Scriptures / written pages' — the same word as ṣuḥuf above (plural of ṣaḥīfa, a written sheet), here without the definite article because it is joined to a following name.

parts.en: genitive ending (here as the first noun of a possessive phrase)

1.grammar: A plural noun standing as the first term of a possessive ('construct') phrase: 'the scriptures OF Abraham…'. The -i ending is genitive: this whole phrase is still governed by the earlier preposition fī ('in the scriptures of…'). It is indefinite in form (no 'al-') precisely because being linked to the names that follow already makes it definite.
1.root: ص-ح-ف (ṣ-ḥ-f) — writing on a page / a written sheet

2.meaning: Abraham (Ibrāhīm) — the name of the prophet. As a proper name it carries no Arabic root meaning.
2.grammar: A proper name in the possessor slot ('scriptures OF Abraham'), so its role is genitive. But foreign/non-Arabic names like this are 'diptotes': they refuse the normal genitive -i and instead take an -a in that position. So the -a you see is doing the job of a genitive here. It also takes no -n (tanwīn) for the same reason.

3.meaning: 'And Moses' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the prophet's name, Mūsā, linking him alongside Abraham as the second figure whose scriptures are mentioned.
3.grammar: The wa- prefix simply means 'and,' joining this name to the previous one ('Abraham and Moses'). It shares the same grammatical role as Abraham — genitive, as the possessor of the scriptures. Like Ibrāhīm, Mūsā is a foreign proper name and therefore a diptote (it would refuse tanwīn and take -a rather than -i); but here no case vowel shows at all, because the name ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) that never changes for case.
